A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same boosting study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison after matching content across revised pagination.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across 20 datasets, including accuracy, sparsity, runtime and base-learner comparisons in Sections 6–7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental outcomes, including the main comparisons and detailed results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: NM-Boost and QRLP-Boost retain their objectives, regularizers and column-generation procedures. Added explanations and the indexing correction in Equation 13 do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 binary-classification datasets: 13 standard benchmarks and seven supplementary datasets. Appendix A retains their populations, tasks and dataset statistics.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged, including LP-Boost, CG-Boost, ERLP-Boost, MD-Boost, Adaboost, XGBoost and LightGBM in the main comparison. Membership also matches within the reweighting, confidence-voting and optimal-tree experiments.

E3.justification: Preprocessing, 60/20/20 splits, hyperparameter grids, tree depths and 100-iteration/45-minute limits are retained. Section 5 adds a rationale for the existing single-hyperparameter sweep, without reporting a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The margin, hyperparameter-sensitivity, sparsity, reweighting, confidence-voting and optimal-tree analyses remain, including their appendix evidence. Reorganized plots do not introduce new analyses or test conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed averaging, standard-deviation error bars and the same significance statements. No new uncertainty-estimation or statistical-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: All experimental table values match, including Tables 1–2 and 6–20. The added 8–15-minute runtime summary restates Table 6. Figure 9 suppresses extreme outliers for visualization, while the corresponding detailed results remain unchanged in Appendix D.6.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Equation 13's index range and adds arguments about sparse LP solutions and QRLP-Boost's strict convexity and unique sample weights under positive initialization. Its new zero-negative-margin description is imprecise for positive margins below the unchanged 1/T offset.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain unchanged: two proposed formulations, the 20-dataset comparison, favorable accuracy–sparsity trade-offs, ensemble reweighting and limitations of optimal-tree boosting.

C2.justification: A new Broader Impact Statement discusses biases in adult and COMPAS, limits their use to benchmarking, and calls for fairness assessment before deployment. It also argues that sparsity aids bias auditing. Section 5 newly frames the retained runtime costs as practical for offline training.

D1.justification: The introduction adds a DOI-based access reference for all experimental results and datasets. Code/package links, the MIT license, software versions, hardware and hyperparameter details were already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain unchanged, including the relationships to earlier LP-based boosting and optimal-tree studies.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited prose expansions in Sections 4–5, adds the Broader Impact Statement, and updates front matter, acknowledgments and some wording. The overall section structure and scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 5–6 regroup panels into dataset columns; Figure 6 changes color encoding and clarifies its legends. Figure 9 narrows its vertical range and discloses omitted extreme outliers. Captions and figure/table placement also change, without a wholesale redesign.

improvement.justification: The results/data archive reference, corrected constraint indexing and clearer comparisons in Figures 5–6 provide a modest overall gain. Benefits are tempered by Figure 9's reduced visibility of extreme cases and imprecise new NM-Boost prose about the offset. The detailed appendix results remain available, and the empirical findings are unchanged.
